corpus_categories.name: Sorting and Order Statistics
corpus_categories.rationale: Dense control flow, data-dependent branching, well-studied mutation space

corpus_categories.name: String Processing and Parsing
corpus_categories.rationale: Character-level data flow; rich DATA dimension variation; off-by-one sensitivity

corpus_categories.name: Graph Algorithms
corpus_categories.rationale: Complex control flow, path-dependent behavior, loop iteration distributions

corpus_categories.name: Numerical / Scientific Computation
corpus_categories.rationale: Numerically sensitive data flow; small mutations change output distributions

corpus_categories.name: Data Structure Operations
corpus_categories.rationale: State transitions are semantically significant; heap topology variation

corpus_categories.name: File and Stream I/O Processing
corpus_categories.rationale: System call patterns and I/O volumes are observationally meaningful

corpus_categories.name: Concurrent / Parallel Programs
corpus_categories.rationale: Thread interleaving, shared-state access; TEMPORAL and EXECUTION dimensions stressed
corpus_categories.note: Determinism enforced via fixed thread count + PRNG seed (Assumption A6)

corpus_categories.name: Cryptographic Primitives
corpus_categories.rationale: Bit-level correctness; high sensitivity to any semantic change; true hard negatives

corpus_categories.name: Compression Algorithms
corpus_categories.rationale: Interplay of DATA, RESOURCE, INTERACTION; known-equivalent implementations across languages

corpus_categories.name: Search and Constraint Satisfaction
corpus_categories.rationale: Backtracking, pruning, solution enumeration; control flow structure is semantically critical

corpus_categories.name: System / OS Interface Programs
corpus_categories.rationale: System call vocabulary, resource usage patterns; exercises INTERACTION and RESOURCE directly

corpus_categories.name: Compiler / Interpreter Front-Ends (Small)
corpus_categories.rationale: Multi-phase control flow with well-defined I/O; known equivalent implementations exist

semantics_preserving_types.name: Rename (Identifier Substitution)
semantics_preserving_types.description: Replace all occurrences of a variable/function name consistently

semantics_preserving_types.name: Comment and Documentation Change
semantics_preserving_types.description: Add, remove, or modify any non-executable annotation

semantics_preserving_types.name: Reorder Independent Statements
semantics_preserving_types.description: Swap two statements with no data dependency

semantics_preserving_types.name: Loop Normalization
semantics_preserving_types.description: Transform for <-> while loops preserving iteration count and body semantics

semantics_preserving_types.name: Constant Folding / Expression Simplification
semantics_preserving_types.description: Replace a constant expression with its pre-computed value

semantics_preserving_types.name: Dead Code Elimination
semantics_preserving_types.description: Remove code that never executes under any reachable input

semantics_preserving_types.name: Extract Method / Inline Method
semantics_preserving_types.description: Refactor code into/out of a function without changing execution semantics

semantics_preserving_types.name: Equivalent Data Structure Substitution
semantics_preserving_types.description: Replace data structure with another providing identical semantics for used operations

semantics_preserving_types.name: Algorithm Substitution (Equivalent Complexity Class)
semantics_preserving_types.description: Replace algorithm with provably output-equivalent alternative

semantics_preserving_types.name: Compiler Optimization Flag Change
semantics_preserving_types.description: Recompile with different optimization flags (e.g., -O0 vs -O2)

semantics_preserving_types.name: Exception Handling Refactor (Equivalent)
semantics_preserving_types.description: Restructure try/catch blocks without changing which exceptions propagate

semantics_preserving_types.name: Logging / Instrumentation Addition (Non-Observable)
semantics_preserving_types.description: Add logging calls that write to a log sink excluded from observable output oracle

semantics_changing_types.name: Off-by-One Error (Boundary Mutation)
semantics_changing_types.description: Change loop bound or array index by +/-1

semantics_changing_types.name: Arithmetic Operator Replacement
semantics_changing_types.description: Replace one binary arithmetic operator with another

semantics_changing_types.name: Wrong Comparison Operator
semantics_changing_types.description: Replace < with <= or == in a semantic comparison

semantics_changing_types.name: Variable Swap (Data Flow Mutation)
semantics_changing_types.description: Replace reference to variable x with reference to variable y at use sites

semantics_changing_types.name: Return Value Change
semantics_changing_types.description: Alter a return statement to return a different value or expression

semantics_changing_types.name: Loop Termination Condition Change
semantics_changing_types.description: Change a loop to terminate early or not on certain inputs

semantics_changing_types.name: Algorithm Logic Mutation (Step Omission)
semantics_changing_types.description: Remove a logically required step from an algorithm

semantics_changing_types.name: Exception Suppression
semantics_changing_types.description: Swallow an exception that should propagate

semantics_changing_types.name: State Initialization Change
semantics_changing_types.description: Alter initial state or variable initialization value

semantics_changing_types.name: Resource Leak Introduction
semantics_changing_types.description: Remove a resource-release call (file close, memory free, lock release)

semantics_changing_types.name: Cross-Language Semantic Port Error
semantics_changing_types.description: Introduce a known semantic difference when porting between languages

ground_truth_method: Four-tier provenance chain: GT-T1 (formal proof, confidence >= 0.999), GT-T2 (exhaustive partition test, confidence >= 0.990), GT-T3 (certified tool + differential test N>=1000, confidence >= 0.950), GT-T4 (broad differential test + expert review, confidence >= 0.900). SC labels additionally require at least one witnessed input discrepancy for hard SC types.

GT-T1.method: Formal equivalence proof (regression verifier, SYMDIFF, Frama-C Wp)
GT-T1.applicability: Simple to moderate C/C++ and Java programs <= 200 LOC

GT-T2.applicability: Programs with finite or symbolically partitionable input spaces

GT-T3.method: Certified transformation tool + N>=1000 differential test
GT-T3.applicability: SP transformations applied by certified tools (compiler, refactoring tool)

GT-T4.method: Broad differential test N>=1000 + expert reviewer + second reviewer for test split
GT-T4.applicability: Complex programs where formal tools are unavailable

validation.purpose: Unbiased intermediate evaluation; frozen after initial population

leakage_prevention: Split assignment at base program level (not pair level)
No base program appears in both train and test
Transformation-symmetric pairs excluded from different splits
Cross-language pairs treated as single units for split assignment
Validation and test splits frozen after initial population

statistical_justification.method: Proportion estimation (Fleiss) + McNemar test power analysis at Bonferroni-corrected alpha = 0.0017
statistical_justification.calculation: Required discordant pairs at alpha=0.0017 = (3.120+0.842)^2 / 1^2 ≈ 15.70; ratio vs alpha=0.05 is 15.70/7.85 = 2.0; 80 discordant × 2 = 160 discordant; at 20% discordance rate: 160/0.20 = 800 total minimum test pairs
statistical_justification.note: Minimum viable test set (800 pairs) is powered for 10% system differences at alpha=0.0017. Recommended test set (1280 pairs) provides margin. Previous alpha=0.05 figure of 400 pairs was insufficient under Bonferroni correction.

determinism_policy.thread_policy: Fixed count + deterministic round-robin for C7 programs
